Let

\[
I=\int_0^{2\pi} e^{\sin(2t)}\sin(\cos(2t))\,dt.
\]

Use the real change of variables \(x=2t\), so \(dt=\frac{dx}{2}\). Then

\[
I=\frac12\int_0^{4\pi} e^{\sin x}\sin(\cos x)\,dx.
\]

Define

\[
f(x)=e^{\sin x}\sin(\cos x).
\]

Since \(f\) is \(2\pi\)-periodic,

\[
\frac12\int_0^{4\pi} f(x)\,dx
=
\int_0^{2\pi} f(x)\,dx.
\]

So it remains to evaluate

\[
\int_0^{2\pi} e^{\sin x}\sin(\cos x)\,dx.
\]

Split this into two intervals:

\[
\int_0^{2\pi} f(x)\,dx
=
\int_0^\pi f(x)\,dx+\int_\pi^{2\pi} f(x)\,dx.
\]

Now use real symmetries.

First, for the interval \([0,\pi]\),

\[
f(\pi-x)
=
e^{\sin(\pi-x)}\sin(\cos(\pi-x)).
\]

Since

\[
\sin(\pi-x)=\sin x,\qquad \cos(\pi-x)=-\cos x,
\]

we get

\[
f(\pi-x)
=
e^{\sin x}\sin(-\cos x)
=
-f(x).
\]

Therefore,

\[
\int_0^\pi f(x)\,dx
=
\int_0^\pi f(\pi-x)\,dx
=
-\int_0^\pi f(x)\,dx,
\]

so

\[
\int_0^\pi f(x)\,dx=0.
\]

Next, for the interval \([\pi,2\pi]\),

\[
f(3\pi-x)
=
e^{\sin(3\pi-x)}\sin(\cos(3\pi-x)).
\]

Using

\[
\sin(3\pi-x)=\sin x,\qquad \cos(3\pi-x)=-\cos x,
\]

we have

\[
f(3\pi-x)
=
e^{\sin x}\sin(-\cos x)
=
-f(x).
\]

Thus,

\[
\int_\pi^{2\pi} f(x)\,dx
=
\int_\pi^{2\pi} f(3\pi-x)\,dx
=
-\int_\pi^{2\pi} f(x)\,dx,
\]

so

\[
\int_\pi^{2\pi} f(x)\,dx=0.
\]

Hence

\[
I=0.
\]
